lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply number properties.
teaching_sequence: Begin with a concrete or familiar situation.
Name the mathematical idea and connect it to prior knowledge.
Model a complete worked example with every step explained.
Move from representation to symbols and then to a new problem.
Ask the learner to explain the method without copying.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain number properties without notes and solve a new example.

items.question: Which approach best helps you understand number properties?
options: Identify what is known, represent it clearly, choose a valid method, and check the result.
Choose an operation before reading the problem.
Copy a worked answer.
Guess and stop.
items.explanation: Understanding the situation, choosing a method and checking the result makes mathematical reasoning reliable.

items.question: Explain number properties as if you were teaching it to someone learning from the basics.
items.answer: A correct response defines number properties, gives a simple example, and explains the reasoning.

items.question: Create and solve a new everyday problem involving number properties.

flashcards.back: Define number properties, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define factors and multiples, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define divisibility, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define number puzzles, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore number properties
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on number properties. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where factors and multiples is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach number puzzles to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
